evidence.claim: BotLab Dynamics designs and sells commercial components that incorporate specific sensory components, notably the BotWing F722 Flight Controller, which includes an integrated ICM42688P Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) / Gyroscope and an integrated DPS310XTSA1 Barometer.
Through their online BotLab Store, the company expands its sensory hardware portfolio to include external navigation modules, specifically marketing the BotNavigator GNSS V1 Drone GPS Module.

According to the product technical datasheets, the flight controllers also feature dedicated I2C interface pads (SDA & SCL), built specifically to extend the sensor ecosystem to external payloads such as magnetometers and sonars.

The integrated sensory processing system on the BotWing F722 Flight Controller is driven by a high-performance STM32F722 Microcontroller (MCU) designed to handle high loop frequencies for fast, real-time sensory data translation.

For navigation sensor refinement, the company uses an RTK (Real-Time Kinematics) GPS system that filters and processes position telemetry data, enabling them to achieve an accuracy of within 10cm compared to the 2m to 5m margin of normal GPS setups.

Their high-frequency radio and sensory links are secured using an onboard Temperature-Compensated Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) in their BotLink 2.4GHz ELRS V1 units, maintaining extreme frequency and telemetry stability across shifting operational environments.

Originally incubated at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi), BotLab Dynamics maintains dedicated in-house technical units across four distinct R&D vectors: animation, PCB design, mechanical design, and simulation.

The company focuses deeply on sensory swarm integration, developing proprietary swarm intelligence and real-time synchronization algorithms that process sensory feedback to prevent collisions across high-density fleets.

Demonstrating its technical scale, the company used its proprietary multi-sensor UAV stack to set a global record by executing a synchronized fleet performance featuring 3,000 drones at the 2025 Mysore Dasara celebrations.

BotLab Dynamics follows an internal vertical integration model, shifting away from off-the-shelf components to manufacture all core hardware components in-house at their facilities, including flight controllers, motor controllers, and GPS modules.
To optimize hardware form factors, the company engineered a specialized solderless architecture for its BotWing F405 flight controller, ensuring clean, modular component integration.

Their system architecture focuses heavily on compact integration, fitting an MCU, ICM42688P IMU, DPS310XTSA1 barometer, and AT7456E OSD into a standardized 30.5mm x 30.5mm mounting footprint weighing just 9.35 grams.

The company designs and flies its platforms under strict adherence to Indian aviation guidelines, actively monitoring and adapting to safety protocols mandated by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).

Their high-frequency radio and sensory links are secured using an onboard Temperature-Compensated Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) in their BotLink 2.4GHz ELRS V1 units, maintaining extreme frequency and telemetry stability across shifting operational environments.
